questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these tests control time and ordering? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What does injecting the clock fixture into ArtifactCache let test_ttl_boundaries do?
choices: Run the TTL checks in separate threads so they finish sooner.
Mock os.utime so the file system is never touched.
Test expiry exactly at and after the TTL without sleeping, because both the stamped mtime and the age calculation come from the same fake time source.

questions.prompt: test_roundtrip fills the cache and a later test uses the cache fixture too. What does the later test see in the cache directory?
choices: The entries left by earlier tests, since the fixture is shared for the session.
An empty directory, because the fixture builds each cache under that test's own tmp_path.
An empty directory only if the earlier test deleted its files.
Whatever entries survive pruning of the earlier test.

questions.prompt: In test_put_replaces_existing_entry_and_refreshes_ttl the second get happens 90 simulated seconds after the first put, with a 60 second TTL, yet it returns b"new". Why?
choices: The TTL is only enforced when the cache is over max_bytes.
get() returns stale entries when the clock moves less than twice the TTL.
The second put rewrote the file and re-stamped its mtime from the clock, so its age is 45 seconds.
The fake clock does not advance during the second advance call.
